Implementation Plan

Scope-mode: Hold Scope  
Reuse-audit: extends `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml` and its existing `SECURITY_AUDIT_FP_EXCLUSIONS` input.  
Scope-mode justification: This is a trust-boundary fix, not a new audit mechanism. Keep the existing override name, but resolve it only to a catalog in the verified support checkout. Under the Core Priorities—Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed—preventing a falsely clean audit takes precedence over preserving audited-branch catalog precedence.

## Planning and automation context

Planning ref: `main` at `56fcde470cc07280e4dfb22b2280be27a34d9d27`. The clarification phase asked no questions; `/answer [auto-answered-by-clarify]` confirms the issue is ready to plan. No integration branch was supplied, so no branch mismatch is established.

Extend the existing `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml` entry point, invoked by its weekly schedule, manual dispatch, or consumer wrapper. No new script, supervisor, database operation, or future-removal registry entry is needed.

## Files likely to change

- `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml` — resolve the configured exclusion catalog against the SHA-verified support checkout before launching the audit; pass its absolute path to the existing script.
- `tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py` — replace the assertion that pins the vulnerable relative-path handoff and add resolution and filtering regressions.
- `README.md` — document the changed trust rule for `SECURITY_AUDIT_FP_EXCLUSIONS`.
- `changelog.d/<issue-number>-trusted-security-audit-exclusions.md` — record the security fix using the repository’s fragment convention.

Leave `workflow-templates/ai-security-audit.yml` unchanged: it already calls the reusable workflow. Leave `scripts/security_audit.sh`’s relative-path behavior unchanged for other callers, including the orchestrator security pass.

## Functions or modules to implement

Add a workflow resolution step that accepts the existing repo-variable value or its default, resolves it to an **absolute, existing regular catalog file in the verified support checkout**, and exports that path as `SECURITY_AUDIT_FP_EXCLUSIONS` for “Run security audit.” Reject missing files, paths escaping the support checkout, and paths into the nested `audit-data` checkout—including traversal and symlink variants. Do not fall back to a catalog in `audit-data`. Keep the configured path out of executable workflow source by passing it through `env:`.

The representative pattern is the workflow’s existing “Create Codex config” step, which passes an absolute catalog path from `${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}` while the audit data remains in a separate checkout.

## Data structures affected

No schema or finding format changes. The existing `SECURITY_AUDIT_FP_EXCLUSIONS` environment variable changes from a potentially relative path to a validated absolute support-catalog path at this workflow’s script invocation.

## API/interface changes

No new endpoint or GitHub API call. Retain the repo-variable name and default. For weekly/manual audits, an override must identify a catalog in the trusted support checkout; an override pointing to the audited repository or elsewhere fails closed.

## Decisions

### D1 — Bind exclusion rules to verified support

- **Chosen:** Resolve and validate the existing override in the reusable workflow, then pass an absolute support-checkout path.
- **Alternatives considered:** Make the audit script prefer support for every caller; remove the override and hard-code the default catalog.
- **Why:** The workflow owns the separate trusted-support and untrusted-data checkouts. This fixes that boundary without changing orchestrator callers or removing an existing identifier.

## Security considerations

The audited branch is untrusted input; the support checkout is pinned to the workflow-approved commit and verified before audit execution. A branch author could otherwise add a valid catch-all exclusion and suppress every finding. Validate both the configured path and its resolved destination so `../audit-data`, absolute paths, and symlinks cannot reintroduce branch-controlled rules. A rejected catalog must fail the run before findings are published, not silently select another file. No new authorization surface is introduced; existing GitHub permissions and target-ref validation remain in force. Do not print credentials or catalog contents in errors.

## Risks and edge cases

Existing consumer configurations that intentionally selected a catalog from the audited repository will now fail until the catalog is placed in trusted support; document this security-driven compatibility change. Test missing and malformed trusted catalogs as failures, and ensure default-branch and explicit-branch audits use the same rule.

**Issue/code conflict:** the issue cites `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml:229`, which is the start of “Run security audit” on this ref; the vulnerable relative exclusion value is passed at line 238. The finding itself is supported by the code.

## Testing considerations

Extend the workflow contract tests to cover the default and a valid trusted override; reject audited-checkout, traversal, outside-absolute, symlink-escape, and missing paths. Add a regression in which `audit-data` contains a valid catch-all catalog but a finding survives filtering with the trusted catalog. Run the focused tests, workflow YAML validation, and the repository’s workflow-file-size guard.

Pre-execution self-check: scope, entry point, trust boundary, compatibility impact, and regression cases are specified; no required scalar input is missing.
